content: The Division of Blood Disorders and Public Health Genomics (DBDPHG) at the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) is dedicated to advancing health, preventing diseases, and addressing health inequities for individuals who are at an increased genetic risk throughout their lives. The goal is to ensure that these individuals have the best possible opportunity to achieve optimal health. There are thousands of inherited genetic disorders that collectively impact millions of individuals in the United States. People living with genetic disorders are more likely to experience a range of challenges, including: Increased susceptibility to health complications. A greater need for specialized medical care. Higher rates of hospitalization. Elevated healthcare costs. The necessity to take time off from work or school. A reduced life expectancy. Furthermore, individuals with genetic disorders often encounter significant barriers to achieving health equity. These barriers are frequently linked to social determinants of health, which are the conditions in the environments where people live, learn, work, and engage in recreational activities. These determinants profoundly influence both health outcomes and overall quality of life. The DBDPHG at the CDC is committed to addressing these challenges by promoting health, preventing disease, and reducing disparities for individuals of all ages who are affected by genetic disorders. Their work aims to ensure that these individuals can lead healthier and more equitable lives.
